plan: This is the first round, so I have no history to learn from. With rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below your value. The exact amount depends on the number of bidders. With 3 bidders, a reasonable strategy is to bid around 2/3 of my value. I will bid slightly below 2/3 of my value to try and win if the other bidders are also bidding rationally. 2/3 of 32 is approximately 21.33. I'll bid $21.3.

Since this is the first round, I have no history to learn from. The optimal bidding strategy in a second-price auction, given the common knowledge of rationality, is to bid slightly below your true value. However, with only one round, the incentive to shade my bid is reduced. I will bid $5.9 to try and win if the other bidders are also shading their bids.

Given that all bidders are rational and have values drawn independently from a uniform distribution between $0 and $49, the optimal bidding strategy is to bid slightly below your true value. In a single-round auction, the Nash Equilibrium strategy is to bid (n-1)/n * value, where n is the number of bidders. In this case, n=3, so the optimal bid is (3-1)/3 * value = (2/3) * value. My value is $17, so my bid should be (2/3) * $17 = $11.33. I will bid $11.3.
